virals_narrative: Dan Koe owned Tuesday: his article 'The most lucrative AI business to start in 2027' hit 514k views and 11.8k bookmarks, the biggest single post on the board in a week, with the thesis that capturing attention is the skill that pays. Sahil Bloom's 'your best years don't have to be behind you' (113k) and James Clear's 'find your purpose for this season' (61k, 660 bookmarks) made reinvention the second theme. Rory Sutherland came back with a burst of ten posts, led by a John Lewis ad read (63k) and Bletchley Park hiring interesting people rather than roles (47k), plus 'jingles never stopped working'. Codie Sanchez's 'you need to be delusional' (33k) and Justin Welsh's 'stop softening what you actually think' (19k) carried the conviction lane. Hormozi, Jack Butcher, David Perell and Sahil Lavingia posted nothing original. Outsiders were stronger than recent days: AI agents as everyday coworkers (Greg Isenberg 199k, Peter Yang 436k) and levelsio's $300/mo solo stack (224k).

drafts.draft_en:
I've watched brilliant musicians die in their bedrooms.

Great ears. Great chops. Nobody knew.

Talent is the ticket.
Attention is the train.

Learn to make people look. A post. A reel. Strangers in your studio on a Sunday.

Then play.
drafts.video_tip: Start on a closed bedroom door, push it open to an empty room with a guitar on the bed. Cut to a full studio table at Ityadi. Say the two middle lines to camera. Under 25 seconds.
drafts.pattern: attention is the business (Dan Koe) + creative career

drafts.draft_en:
Stop hunting for your life's purpose.

Find this season's.

Right now mine is wool, a tufting gun and strangers making their first rug at Ityadi.

Before that, films. Before that, music.

Each season paid for the next.

Pick one. Burn your bum on it. Move.
drafts.video_tip: Three quick cuts of objects from each season: an old film slate or hard drive, a keyboard, then the tufting gun firing into cloth. Voiceover reads the post. End on a hand pulling a finished rug off the frame.
drafts.pattern: purpose for this season (James Clear, Sahil Bloom) + creative career

drafts.draft_en:
Jingles never stopped working.
They just stopped being cool.

Seven notes and a brand name, and people hum it in the shower twenty years later.

Show me the reel that does that.

Unfashionable is not dead.
Use what works. Let the others chase the trend.
drafts.video_tip: Sit at the keyboard and play one famous old Indian jingle from memory, no intro. Turn to camera and say the first two lines. Burn the last line in as a caption.

drafts.draft_en:
Every soft version of my work got polite nods.

Every sharp version got me my people.

Say the thing plainly. The ones who flinch were never yours.

Safe is just forgettable in a nicer costume.

Say it straight.
drafts.video_tip: Hold up two prints or rugs side by side, one beige and safe, one loud. Point at each on the first two lines. Single take, no music.
drafts.pattern: stop softening (Justin Welsh, Codie Sanchez) + creative business
